types.name: AccelerationStructure
types.doc:
Hardware ray-tracing acceleration structure. BLAS wraps one
triangle geometry read straight from existing GPU vertex/index buffers
(positions must be float3 at the start of each vertex); TLAS gathers
BLAS instances with 3x4 row-major transforms — the same value layout
ray-tracing APIs expect, i.e. the upper three rows of the engine's
row-major Mat4. Builds are synchronous (single-time command buffer).
A TLAS created with allowUpdate=true keeps its instance/scratch buffers
alive and can be REFIT in place via RefitTLAS when only transforms
changed: same instance count, same BLAS set — orders of magnitude
cheaper than a full rebuild for a moving scene.
Requires RendererCapabilities::SupportsRayQuery.

members.doc:

Valid only on a TLAS built with allowUpdate=true and an identical
instance count; returns false when the caller must rebuild instead.

types.name: FBlasCompactionSettings
types.doc:
BLAS compaction policy (r.RT.BLASCompaction).

A bottom-level acceleration structure is allocated from the driver's
conservative pre-build estimate, which is routinely 40-60% larger than what
the finished structure occupies. Both APIs can report the real figure after
the build (VK_QUERY_TYPE_ACCELERATION_STRUCTURE_COMPACTED_SIZE_KHR /
EmitRaytracingAccelerationStructurePostbuildInfo) and copy the structure
into a right-sized allocation, and on a scene with a few hundred meshes
that is tens of megabytes of VRAM the ray scene was holding for nothing.

The copy is a second GPU submit, so it needs a budget: the engine already
spreads BLAS BUILDS over frames (r.RTScene.BlasBudget) precisely because a
burst of synchronous submits is a hitch, and compaction must not undo that
by doubling the burst. Over budget, a structure simply stays uncompacted —
there is no queue that could compact it later, because the moment a TLAS
records its address a copy would strand every structure referencing the old
one. Compaction therefore happens between the build's fence signalling and
the structure being handed to the caller, which is the only window in which
nothing can be pointing at it yet.

Everything that decides is a pure function over the build-complete events,
so the policy is testable with no device (--rt-compaction-test).

members.name: MinSavingPercent
members.doc:
A copy that reclaims almost nothing still costs a submit and a second
allocation, and a driver that already sizes its BLASes tightly reports
exactly that.

members.name: InFrameBuilds
members.doc:
r.RT.InFrameBuilds: a build made while a frame list records is recorded
into that list instead of a single-time submit plus fence wait (a stall
per BLAS, per TLAS rebuild). The compacted size is only known once that
frame has executed, by which time the TLAS recorded right after it holds
the address — so in-frame builds stay uncompacted, and the memory is the
price of not stalling. Builds outside a frame (level load) still compact.

members.name: Refittable

types.name: EFrameGenBackend
types.doc:
Which frame-interpolation backend answers r.FrameGeneration. FSR3 is the AMD
ffx-api proxy swapchain (always the fallback); DLSSG is NVIDIA DLSS Frame
Generation over Streamline (sl.dlss_g); XeSSFG is Intel XeSS Frame Generation
(libxess_fg.dll). DLSSG/XeSSFG are dynamic-loaded and capability-gated —
reported unsupported until their runtime + a supporting GPU are present.
MetalFX is Apple's MTLFXFrameInterpolator — the only backend on macOS,
always linked, probed per-device at runtime (needs the macOS 26 runtime;
r.FrameGeneration.Backend preference is ignored there, MetalFX either
answers or nothing does).

Monotonic rendered-frame counter — Streamline tokens and the FG SDKs

members.name: displayWidth
members.doc:
Presented backbuffer size. DLSS-G's colour dimensions are the swapchain
the interpolator reads, NOT the render resolution — configuring it with
the render size undershot the minimum-resolution check and mis-sized
every optical-flow allocation. 0 = unknown (backends fall back to the
render size).

members.name: viewToClip
members.doc:
Camera matrices, row-major, column-vector convention (v' = M * v),
UNJITTERED — the same contract as UpscalerResolveDesc. Streamline
derives clipToPrevClip/prevClipToClip for the interpolator from these;
Identity degrades to the static-camera assumption. FSR3/XeSS-FG/MetalFX
ignore them (they take the camera basis fields above instead).

members.name: IsSupported
members.doc:
True when frame generation CAN run on this machine with ANY backend (FSR3
ffx-api DLL loadable + distinct present/acquire queues, or a supported DLSS-G). The
r.FrameGeneration toggle is a silent no-op when false.

members.name: IsBackendSupported
members.doc:
Whether a specific backend can run right now — the editor greys the ones
that can't. FSR3 needs the ffx-api DLL + present/acquire queues distinct
from the game queue (from ANY family — Vulkan takes spare compute queues
on AMD/Intel, D3D12 creates its own command queues); DLSS-G needs
the Streamline runtime and MOWO_DLSSG_ENABLED (false until vendored).

members.name: ActiveBackend
members.doc:
The backend that will actually run given r.FrameGeneration.Backend and
availability (None when frame generation can't run at all). This is the
WANTED backend: after a cvar change it answers the new choice one frame
before the swapchain recreate moves presentation over. Per-frame present
contracts (UiCompositedByEngine) read the live latch instead.

members.name: BackendName
members.doc: Human-readable backend name for stats / the settings UI.

members.name: IsActive
members.doc:
True while generated frames are actually being presented — the answer
for stats and the settings UI. Toggled via the r.FrameGeneration console
variable (the swapchain recreates at the next BeginFrame). DLSS-G only
reads true here once Streamline reports more than one presented frame
per rendered one, so this must never gate the feed — see WantsInputs.

members.name: WantsInputs
members.doc:
True while a frame-generation present path is BUILT and waiting for its
per-frame inputs: the swapchain was created through the backend's
interpolator and the scene owns it. This, not IsActive, gates Prepare.
DLSS-G starts presenting generated frames only after it has been fed
(FrameGenSetActive runs inside Prepare), so gating the feed on
"presenting" held it off forever on D3D12 and Vulkan. Falls back to
IsActive on a backend without the entry.

members.name: SetSceneOwnsSwapchain
members.doc:
Frame generation only engages while the presented swapchain shows the
scene directly — the standalone runtime, or a fullscreen play session.
The editor composites its viewport as a texture inside the Arc UI, so
interpolating that swapchain would warp the whole editor, not just the 3D
view. The runtime opts in; the editor leaves it off and r.FrameGeneration
is a no-op there. Defaults to off.

members.name: Prepare
members.doc:
Record this frame's interpolation inputs into the current command
buffer and (re)configure the generator. Call once per rendered frame
from the PRIMARY view after motion vectors are produced; no-op while
inactive.

members.name: SetUiImage
members.doc:
Register this frame's UI overlay (HUD-less compositing): the proxy
swapchain composites `ui` — a display-sized, premultiplied-alpha RGBA
image — onto BOTH the rendered and the generated frame at present
time, so UI pixels never pass through the interpolator (no ghosting).
The backbuffer the app presents must then be scene-only. Call once per
rendered frame while the main command buffer records; pass nullptr to
clear the registration (UI composited into the backbuffer is
interpolated with the scene again). No-op while inactive.

members.name: UiCompositedByEngine
members.doc:
Whether the app must KEEP compositing the HUD into the backbuffer
while a UI image is registered. MetalFX has no proxy that composites
UI at present time — the registered image is the interpolator's
anti-ghosting mask and the backbuffer still carries the HUD. DLSS-G
works the same way: Streamline interpolates the presented backbuffer
(HUD included) and the registered image is tagged as UIColorAndAlpha
so generated frames recompose UI pixels instead of warping them.
FSR3/XeSS-FG follow the HUD-less contract above: scene-only
backbuffer, the proxy composites the UI onto both frames itself
(drawing it into the backbuffer too would double-composite).
Answers for the backend PRESENTING this frame (latched at Prepare),
not the wanted one — the two disagree for the one frame between a
backend cvar change and the swapchain recreate.

members.name: GetPresentCount
members.doc:
Images the proxy swapchain has presented since creation — rendered +
generated, so about the multiplier times the rendered frame count while
generation keeps up. 0 while inactive. Stats/verification.

members.name: GetMaxMultiplier
members.doc:
The largest output multiplier the live backend (or, with none live, the
wanted one) reports for this GPU (DLSS 4 Multi Frame Generation reaches
4x, DLSS 4.5 6x, XeSS-FG what the driver says). 2 until that backend has
published a larger one; FSR3 and MetalFX generate one frame and stay at 2.

members.name: GetEffectiveMultiplier
members.doc:
The multiplier generation runs at: r.FrameGeneration.Multiplier clamped
to GetMaxMultiplier, so asking a 2x GPU for 4x degrades to 2x instead
of failing the vendor call.

members.name: IsDynamicMultiplierSupported
members.doc: DLSS-G dynamic mode (varies the multiplier toward a target frame rate).

types.name: FrameGenerationControls
types.doc:
Shared frame-generation control state. The r.FrameGeneration /
r.FrameGeneration.Backend console variables, the scene-owns-swapchain flag
and the preference-fallback backend selection are registered/stored ONCE
here in the RHI module — every backend DLL (Vulkan, D3D12) reads the same
state instead of re-registering MakeConsoleVar statics per module.

members.name: GetToggle
members.doc:
r.FrameGeneration: 0 = off, 1 = on. Backends read it every BeginFrame
and write 0 back when a vendor failure forces generation off. GetToggle
answers 0 while the auto-hold below keeps generation off.

members.name: UpdateAutoHold
members.signature: static void UpdateAutoHold(double frameIntervalMs, float refreshHz, bool vsync, double nowSeconds)
members.doc:
Auto-hold (r.FrameGeneration.AutoHold, default on). Under VSync the
display refresh caps the PRESENTED rate, so a scene that already renders
at the refresh gains nothing from interpolation: measured 2026-10-13 on a
120 Hz panel, rendered 117 -> 60 fps, presented 117 -> 120, latency
doubled. The host feeds the rendered frame interval every frame; while
generation is requested the policy first measures the base rate with
generation held off and engages only when that rate stays clearly below
the refresh. Once engaged it stays engaged until the request changes —
the base rate cannot be measured while generating, and every switch
recreates the swapchain.

members.name: GetBackendPreference
members.doc:

1 = FSR3, 2 = DLSS-G, 3 = XeSS-FG.

a given GPU — Reflex needs NVIDIA, Anti-Lag 2 an AMD driver, XeLL an Intel
one — so Auto simply takes whichever this device runs, the way UE's "Low
Latency" setting picks by vendor. A live frame generator overrides the pick
with the runtime it depends on: DLSS-G requires Reflex, XeSS-FG XeLL.

r.LowLatency.Backend: 0 = auto (whichever this GPU runs), 1 = Reflex,
2 = Anti-Lag 2, 3 = XeLL. A preference the device cannot run falls back
to Auto.

members.name: IsBackendSupported
members.doc: Whether a runtime can drive this device right now (DLL + driver + GPU).

members.name: ActiveBackend
members.doc:
The runtime the per-frame sleep and markers go to, given the preference
and what this device supports. None when no runtime answers.

members.signature: static ELowLatencyBackend SelectBackend(int preference, bool reflex, bool antiLag2, bool xell)

Pure selection shared by every backend: the preference when it is

types.name: EReflexMarker
types.doc:
The points a low-latency runtime wants the frame bracketed at. NVIDIA's PCL
markers and Intel's XeLL markers define the same six in the same order, so a
backend maps this by value; nothing here is vendor-specific.

types.name: Reflex
types.doc:
The per-frame low-latency interface. Historically NVIDIA Reflex only (the
name stayed); it now drives whichever runtime LowLatency::ActiveBackend
picks — Reflex through Streamline (sl.reflex + sl.pcl) on D3D12, D3D11 and
Vulkan, and on D3D12 also AMD Anti-Lag 2 and Intel XeLL. DLSS-G requires
Reflex low-latency to be active. Every entry is a no-op when no runtime
answers on this GPU, and on macOS (Metal registers none of it).

Setting the mode alone reduces nothing: the driver needs the per-frame Sleep
to hold the CPU back and the markers to know where the frame's phases are.
Renderer::BeginFrame / EndFrame / Present drive both — the RHI's own frame
boundaries — so no application code has to remember to.

members.name: SetMode
members.doc: 0 = off, 1 = low latency, 2 = low latency + boost.

members.name: GetMode
members.doc:
The mode last handed to SetMode. Sleep/SetMarker short-circuit on it, so
a build with no Reflex at all pays one integer compare per marker.

members.name: IsSupported
members.doc: Whether Reflex can run on this GPU/driver right now.

members.name: SetFrameLimit
members.doc:
Presented-frame rate cap enforced by the driver (sl::ReflexOptions::
frameLimitUs), 0 = none. It works with the low-latency mode off, and the
driver paces the frame instead of a CPU sleep after present, which is the
latency the sleep adds. Re-applied immediately when it changes.

members.name: IsFrameLimitActive
members.doc:
True when the cap is being enforced by Reflex, so the engine's own frame
pacing must stand down rather than stack a second limiter on it.

members.name: Sleep
members.doc:
The driver-controlled CPU sleep that paces the frame. Call once, at the
very top of the frame, before any of its work. `frameIndex` must be the
monotonic Renderer::GetFrameCounter value the rest of the frame's vendor
calls use.

members.name: SetMarker
members.signature: static void SetMarker(EReflexMarker marker, uint64_t frameIndex)
members.doc:
Bracket a frame phase. Thread-safe by the vendor contract, so the
deferred-present path can mark from the RHI thread as long as it passes
the frame index its work belongs to.

members.name: GetLatencyMs
members.doc:
End-to-end latency of the newest completed frame report, milliseconds
(simulation start → GPU render end). 0 when Reflex is off, unsupported,
or no report has landed yet. This is the ONLY observable the plumbing
has: on a machine without an NVIDIA GPU it stays 0 by design.

types.name: FGpuBreadcrumbs
types.doc:
GPU breadcrumbs: every MOWO_GPU_SCOPE writes its id into a small
host-visible marker buffer from the GPU timeline — one slot at scope
begin ("last started") and one at scope end ("last completed"). The
mapped memory survives a device loss, so when the GPU falls over the
crash log names the pass that was in flight instead of a bare
DEVICE_LOST. This class owns the backend-free half: the id→name ring
and the loss report; each backend registers a reader for its marker
buffer and records the actual writes inside Begin/EndGpuScope.

members.name: RegisterScope
members.doc:
Ring-registers a scope name (string literals only — the pointer is
stored, not copied) and returns its nonzero marker id.

members.name: SetGpuReader
members.doc:
Backend hookup: readers return the marker slots' current contents
(0 when the buffer never got written).

members.name: SetFaultDescriber
members.doc:
The driver's own account of the loss: D3D12 DRED (the command list and
operation that faulted, the page-fault address and the resources that
lived or recently died there) or Vulkan VK_EXT_device_fault. It is
appended to the report, which is logged before the fatal crash dump
copies the log, so it reaches the player's crash report.

members.name: DescribeLoss
members.doc:
The text ReportDeviceLost logs — breadcrumbs, then the fault
description. Split out so it can be checked without losing a device.

members.name: ReportDeviceLost
members.doc:
Called from the backend error macros on a device-loss result. Logs
the report once per process — the cascade of failing calls after a
loss must not spam it — and tags the crash report (gpu_lost_scope,
gpu_fault) so the backend can group losses by pass.

members.name: WasDeviceLost
members.doc:
True once any backend reported a loss. The frame loop ends on it and the
host exits non-zero: a run that lost its device used to exit 0 and write
plausible --metrics, which a harness read as a fast successful run.

Ran on the async-compute queue, overlapping the graphics scopes: its

members.name: cpuBeginTracyTime
members.doc:
When the frame began recording on the CPU, on Tracy's clock (0 without
Tracy) and a steady clock in nanoseconds. Scope times are offsets from
the frame's first timestamp query, so these are what place them on a
profiler timeline.

types.name: GpuTimings
types.doc:
Read accessor for the most-recently resolved GPU frame (a few frames
behind real time). Delegates to the active backend's timers.

members.name: IsRecordingEnabled
members.doc:
Whether GPU scopes record timestamps. Off, a scope still names its span
for a capture and writes the crash breadcrumb, but takes no timestamp
pair, so the resolve (which BLOCKS on Vulkan) never has a slot to read.
Driven by r.GpuTimings — armed by default in a build that carries
asserts, off in profile and release, and movable at runtime either way,
because the per-pass breakdown is how most of this pass was found.

members.name: AreMarkersEnabled
members.doc:
Whether a scope also emits a debug marker the capture tools show: a
PIX event on D3D12/D3D11, a VK_EXT_debug_utils label on Vulkan, a
debug group on Metal. r.GpuMarkers, default on: a marker is one small
command and a capture without pass names is unreadable.

members.name: SetRecordingEnabled
members.doc:
Hold recording on for half a second without touching the cvar. A panel
that displays the breakdown calls this every frame it draws; one that
closes simply stops, and the cost lapses with it.

members.name: RequestFrameTime
members.doc:
Hold the frame's GPU total on for half a second without arming the
per-pass breakdown: only the outermost scopes take timestamps, so
LastResolvedFrame().totalMs stays live in profile and release where
r.GpuTimings is 0. Dynamic resolution calls it every frame it steers —
it used to read a total nobody recorded and never moved the scale.

members.name: ShouldRecordScope
members.doc:
What a backend asks before it opens a timestamp pair: everything while
recording is on, only a scope with nothing timed open around it while a
frame total is requested. openDepth counts the scopes the backend's
timers actually opened, so a skipped child never reads as a parent.

members.name: BusyMs
members.doc:
The time the GPU spent inside the frame's outermost scopes, summed —
what the frame costs. totalMs spans the first timestamp to the last and
also counts every bubble in between (a split submit waiting on the
CPU, a copy-queue wait), which is time a lower resolution does not buy
back. 0 when the frame carries no outermost scope.

members.name: StampFrameBegin
members.signature: static void StampFrameBegin(int64_t& tracyTime, int64_t& steadyNs)
members.doc:
Stamps both clocks for a frame about to record its first scope. Every
backend's timers call it from BeginFrame and carry the stamp through to
the resolved frame.

members.name: PublishToTracy
members.doc:
Sends a newly resolved frame's scopes to Tracy's GPU timeline, one
context for every backend. A no-op without Tracy or with no profiler
connected. Renderer::EndFrame calls it.

members.name: kMaxScopesPerFrame
members.doc:
Scope budget per frame, shared by every backend's query pool. Runtime/Game
alone opens 69 in a frame; at the 64 this used to be, the tail of the
breakdown vanished with no diagnostic, so the cheapest-looking passes were
the ones that never reported.

types.name: GpuScope
types.doc:
Backend-agnostic GPU-scope RAII: brackets a pass with two GPU timestamps
on the current command buffer. Consumers (SceneRenderer's 20 passes)
drop their raw command-buffer handles + the backend timer/profiler
headers and just write `MOWO_GPU_SCOPE("Lighting")`. The scope resolves
the active command buffer and backend timers internally, so this stays
the single backend-free recording surface; another backend slots in
behind it.

Tracy GPU zones are a separate, build-gated concern living in the modules
that enable Tracy.

types.name: FHdrMetadata
types.doc:
Mastering metadata an HDR swapchain hands the compositor and the display:
the primaries and white point of the signal's container, the luminance range
it was graded for, and the brightest pixel / brightest frame average it will
carry. Without it Windows HDR and gamescope guess the range and either clip
highlights or tone-map the whole image dim. Chromaticities are CIE 1931 xy,
luminances in nits.

members.name: ForOutput
members.signature: static FHdrMetadata ForOutput(int32_t activeHdrMode, float maxNits, float paperWhiteNits)
members.doc:
From the active output mode (1 = scRGB, 2 = HDR10; 0 = SDR, which
carries none) and the existing r.HDRMaxNits / r.HDRPaperWhiteNits. The
tonemapper never writes past the peak, so it is both the mastering peak
and MaxCLL; paper white is the level a frame sits at on average.

members.name: SupportsAsyncCompute
members.doc:
Async compute lane: a SECOND hardware queue that runs compute work
concurrently with the graphics queue. The engine records into it by
swapping which command buffer the facade hands the RHI (see
Renderer::BeginAsyncCompute), so nothing below this interface changes.
Ordering is one-way and explicit: the lane signals on submit, the
graphics queue waits before the first pass that reads what it wrote.
A backend without a second queue reports false and the caller records
inline instead — same results, no overlap.

members.name: WaitAsyncComputeOnGraphics
members.doc:
Order the graphics queue behind the lane's last submission. allowSplit
says whether the backend may CLOSE the graphics command buffer here,
submit what is recorded so far and continue on a fresh one — the only
way a queue whose wait is a submit-level operation (Vulkan semaphores,
D3D12 queue fences) gets the work recorded BEFORE this point to run
concurrently with the lane. It is false while a render pass or a GPU
timestamp scope is open, because both hold the raw command buffer the
split would end underneath them; the backend must then fall back to a
wait on the frame's own submit, which is still correct and merely
gives up the in-frame overlap.

members.name: SupportsGraphicsToLaneHandoff
members.doc:
The REVERSE direction: the graphics queue signals, the lane's submit
waits. Lifting scheduling rule 1 for a single pass needs exactly this,
and it is a second value space on purpose — sharing the lane's timeline
would let a lane signal satisfy a graphics wait and vice versa.

SignalGraphicsHandoffForLane closes the graphics segment recorded so
far, submits it with NO wait of its own, and signals the hand-off value
the next SubmitAsyncCompute will wait on. It has the same command-buffer
precondition as the split wait (no open render pass, no open GPU scope)
and returns false when it could not run — the caller must then not open
the lane, because a lane opened without the hand-off reads this frame's
graphics output mid-write.

active backend casts them internally) so this header stays SDK/backend-free.

(dynamic resolution renders into a top-left subrect): renderWidth/Height is
the valid extent, the image's own dimensions are the allocation, and
`output` is OUTPUT resolution and always fully valid.

vectors; the spatial/None/TAA paths ignore this and return false from
Resolve() so the renderer keeps its existing present-time upscale.

members.name: preExposure
members.doc:
Exposure handoff. `color` carries scene radiance ALREADY multiplied by
preExposure — the engine's normalization scalar (r.PreExposure), which
slews by up to 5% per frame while eye adaptation moves. A vendor
upscaler told nothing reads that slew as a real luminance change and its
history pumps with the adaptation; preExposure is the value to divide
back out (FSR's dispatch field, DLSS's option of the same name).
exposureScale is the multiplier that takes the buffer AS GIVEN to
display-referred luminance — the tonemapper's own factor, auto-exposure
included, already divided by preExposure — which is what an SDK with an
internal tonemapper (XeSS) wants. Both default to 1.0 = "not
pre-exposed, unit exposure", which is what every caller that leaves them
alone means.

members.name: frameIndex
members.doc:

members.name: invViewProj
members.doc:
Camera reprojection matrices, row-major, for TSR's zero-velocity fallback
(sky/holes get no per-object motion vector). UNJITTERED, matching the
velocity pass: a jittered pair puts the per-frame jitter delta into the
fallback reprojection and the accumulated history wobbles with the
Halton sequence. Plain float arrays so this header keeps its no-Math,
no-SDK dependency set. Identity = no camera motion, which is exactly
what a synthetic static frame wants. FSR ignores them (its SDK
reprojects internally); the DLSS backends transpose them (with
worldToView/viewToClip below) into sl::Constants' clip-to-prev-clip
pair and camera basis.

members.name: diffuseAlbedo
members.doc:
Optional denoiser aux inputs — all default null, so existing backends
are untouched. Consumed ONLY by the Metal backend today: when
r.MetalFX.Denoised is on, the device supports
MTLFXTemporalDenoisedScaler and diffuseAlbedo/normals/roughness are
set, the MetalFX resolve runs Apple's denoised temporal scaler
(denoise + upscale in one pass over the stochastic RT effects)
instead of the plain temporal scaler; with any of them null (or the
cvar off, or an unsupported device) it behaves exactly as before.
FSR/XeSS/TSR/TAA/Spatial ignore every field below; DLSS reads only the
worldToView/viewToClip matrices at the bottom.
Engine fill (SceneRendererPost): diffuseAlbedo = GBuffer RT0 (RGBA8,
albedo.rgb + metallic.a); normals = roughness = GBuffer RT1 (RGBA16F,
world normal.xyz + roughness.a) with roughnessChannel = 3 telling the
backend which channel of the roughness image carries the scalar (the
Metal backend swizzles it into R via a texture view). specularAlbedo
has no engine producer yet and stays null — backends approximate it
from diffuseAlbedo. reactiveMask is the engine's R8 responsiveness mask
(SceneRenderer's pre-translucency diff, r.ReactiveMask) — TSR reads it
directly, FSR takes it as `reactive`, DLSS as the BiasCurrentColorHint
tag and XeSS as its responsive-pixel mask; null means "no mask", which
every backend degrades to cleanly. denoiseStrengthMask is plumbed for
later authoring, always null today.

members.doc: 0=R 1=G 2=B 3=A within `roughness`

members.name: worldToView
members.doc:
Camera basis for the denoised resolve's specular reprojection.
Row-major storage, column-vector convention (v' = M * v — the same
P * V composition UpdateFrameUniforms builds), UNJITTERED projection
like the pair above. Identity = not provided; the Metal denoised path
and the DLSS constants fill (projection + camera basis/position) read
them.

members.name: ReadbackLayered

at the image's native format (RGBA16F, RGBA32F, RGBA8, ...). Unlike

layout Image2D::CreateWithMips / UploadMipRange consume, so a cube
reconstructs by pointing one MipData per mip into this blob. Caller owns
the returned buffer (delete[]); outSize = the total byte count.

One resource a compiled shader binds, in the abstract (set, binding)
space the layouts are declared in. Vulkan reads it off the SPIR-V
decorations; D3D12 joins the bindmap rows with the DXIL PSV0 usage
table; D3D11 joins the bindmap rows with D3DReflect.

members.name: AcceptedTypes
members.doc:
Bitmask over DescriptorType (FPipelineBindingValidation::TypeBit) of
every layout type this resource may legitimately be declared as. SPIR-V
is exact; a D3D register class is coarser (a t register backs a
texture, a structured SRV or a TLAS), so the adapter widens the mask
rather than guessing.

members.name: Structured
members.doc:
StructuredBuffer<T> / RWStructuredBuffer<T>: the D3D backends encode
T's stride in the buffer view, so a row that lost its stride binds a
raw view the shader reads as zeros.

members.signature: static std::vector<FPipelineBindingIssue> Check(const std::vector<FReflectedShaderBinding>& reflected, const std::vector<DescriptorSetLayoutDescription>& layouts, bool hasBindlessTable)
members.doc:
Pure decision: reflected bindings against the layouts a spec declares.
Layouts are matched by vector position (the backends build set N from
DescriptorSetLayouts[N]); a bindless table occupies the set right after
the declared ones.

members.signature: static void Merge(std::vector<FReflectedShaderBinding>& into, const FReflectedShaderBinding& binding)
members.doc:
Folds one stage's reflection into a pipeline-wide list: a slot two
stages share (a UBO the VS and PS both read) is one binding.

members.name: Escalates
members.doc:
--gpu-validation / --sync-validation: the GPU rows run under it and
their validation-flat gates must see the mismatch as an error.

members.name: Report
members.signature: static void Report(const char* backendTag, const std::string& pipelineName, const std::vector<FPipelineBindingIssue>& issues)
members.doc:
WARN per issue naming backend, pipeline, set and binding; ERROR when
Escalates().

members.name: AdmitRecorded
members.signature: static bool AdmitRecorded(const char* backendTag, const std::string& pipelineName, const std::vector<FPipelineBindingIssue>& issues, uint64_t recordedKey)
members.doc:
The backends' entry point. A live pipeline (recordedKey 0) reports as
above and is always built. A pipeline rebuilt from a PSO-cache record
whose layouts no longer cover its shader is refused: the record is
marked stale (FPsoCache drops it on the next write) and the caller
returns without building — the renderer creates the current layout
itself, so prewarming the stale one only bought ~160 warnings a run.

members.name: ReportedIssueCount
members.doc:
Every issue Report has ever described, process-wide. A warning nobody
reads is how the software rasteriser's resolve shipped for a month with a
declared binding missing from its layout, and a comment above the layout
saying so did not stop it — a test asserting this is zero after the
pipelines it cares about exist does. Cleared by ResetReportedIssueCount
so a row can measure one span.

walk is a hundred lines and this stays device-free for the test host.

members.name: Flush
members.doc:
Write the session's recording to <ProjectSavedDir>/PsoCache/PsoCache.mdfb.
Merges over an existing file (a recording grows across sessions), keeps
records deduplicated by content hash. No-op with nothing recorded or no
project open. Called from Renderer::Shutdown.

members.name: WriteSessionMerged
members.doc:
Writes this session's records merged over whatever `file` holds — the
gather tool's way of growing the committed bundle (Config/PsoCache.mdfb)
without going through one developer's recording. Returns the record count
the file holds afterwards, 0 when nothing was written.

members.name: Prewarm
members.signature: static uint32_t Prewarm(const std::filesystem::path& file, const std::function<void(uint32_t done, uint32_t total)>& progress = {})
members.doc:
Re-create every pipeline recorded in `file` (throwaway refs — the
side effect on the driver/backend caches is the product). Returns the
number of pipelines created; a record the backend refused as stale
(NoteStaleRecord) is not counted. Requires an initialized Renderer. The
compiles run in parallel where the backend compiles asynchronously;
`progress` is called on the calling thread as they finish (done, total),
which is how a loading screen shows them.

members.name: StartupCachePath
members.doc:
What a starting game prewarms from: the recording a package ships, else
the project's own development recording, so a dev run after a shader
rebuild compiles its pipelines up front instead of across the first frames.

members.name: BundledCachePath
members.doc:
The staged recording a packaged game prewarms from, resolved against
the executable's working directory. Empty if absent.

members.name: NoteStaleRecord
members.doc:
A backend refused a prewarmed pipeline because the record's layouts no
longer cover its shader (the recording predates a binding the shader
gained). The record is excluded from every later write of the recording,
so it stops coming back each run. Thread-safe: async builds call it.

types.name: RHIViewport
types.doc:
One OS window's presentation surface — the UE5 FRHIViewport analog. Owns a
per-window swapchain (surface / backbuffer / depth / sync, all already held
by SwapChain) plus its own command buffer, and drives its own
BeginFrame -> record -> EndFrame -> Present cycle independently of the main
window. Because IDynamicRHI takes the SwapChain and command buffer per call,
this is backend-agnostic composition — no per-API subclass. The main window
is viewport 0; secondary windows (crash reporter, tear-off tabs, tool
windows) each get their own.

members.doc:
Create a viewport owning a brand-new swapchain + command buffer for
spec.NativeWindowHandle. Used for secondary / tool windows.

members.signature: static Ref<RHIViewport> CreateMain(Ref<SwapChain> swapChain, Ref<RenderCommandBuffer> commandBuffer)

Adopt the main window's already-created swapchain + command buffer as
viewport 0, so the existing main-loop path stays byte-for-byte unchanged.

members.name: BeginFrame

already put there — the main window's submit above all, which renders
the images a secondary window samples. Runs inline without an RHI thread.

secondary window), false for the adopted main viewport.

members.name: MarkGpuRetired

command buffer are destroyed without a device-wide idle wait.

types.name: FRayTracingHitGroup
types.doc:
One shader-binding-table hit record. Entry names are the exported
function names inside the RT library blob (the `[shader("closesthit")]`
/ `[shader("anyhit")]` functions). An empty name means the group has no
shader of that kind — a shadow-ray group is legitimately any-hit only,
traced with RAY_FLAG_SKIP_CLOSEST_HIT_SHADER.

members.name: Library
members.doc:
ONE library blob (`<name>.rt.spv` / `.rt.dxil`) carrying every entry
point below. Both APIs want the whole RT program as one module, so a
per-stage Shader would have to be taken apart again.

members.name: HitGroups
members.doc:
Index i here is SBT hit-group i, which is what
AccelerationStructure::Instance::SbtHitGroupIndex selects. A consumer
that builds this from the material models its frame actually submits
gets a per-material table; one that ships a single entry gets the
whole scene funnelled through it, because every instance that never
set the field selects 0.

members.name: MaxPayloadSize
members.doc:
Bytes. Both backends need these declared up front (VkRayTracingPipeline
interface create info / D3D12_RAYTRACING_SHADER_CONFIG) and an
under-declared payload is silent corruption, not a validation error on
every driver.

members.name: MaxAttributeSize
members.doc: built-in triangle barycentrics = 8

members.name: MaxRecursionDepth
members.doc:
1 = the raygen traces, hits never trace again. Raising it costs stack
on every backend, so it stays at what the program actually recurses.

members.name: BindlessTable
members.doc:
The table a hit shader samples material textures through, appended as
descriptor set index DescriptorSetLayouts.size() — the same convention
the graphics and compute specs use. A hit shader has no per-material
descriptor set to reach: traversal picks the SHADER, and the record it
dispatches through carries only an identifier, so an alpha mask that is
not in a bindless table is not addressable from a hit at all. Null on a
device without descriptor indexing, and the consumer's hit groups then
have to make do with what the per-instance record already carries.
Bind() points the pipeline at it — there is no separate bind call.

members.name: UsesRawBuffers
members.doc:
The library calls MOWO_RAW_LOAD / MOWO_RAW_STORE (vertex/index fetch by
handle). On Vulkan those are buffer device addresses and need no
descriptor at all; on D3D12 they resolve through the global raw-buffer
tables, whose root parameters every other pipeline infers from the
DXIL's PSV0 resource rows — which a lib_6_3 library blob does not carry
in the form that pass reads. Left false on a library that raw-loads,
D3D12's CreateStateObject rejects the program outright for an uncovered
register space, so the consumer falls back rather than misreading.

members.name: splitBeginAfter
members.doc:
Execution-order index of the last pass that touched the resource before
this transition, set only when other passes lie between that pass and
the one this barrier precedes: the transition may then BEGIN right after
that pass and END here. RG_INVALID = one whole barrier, here.

types.doc:
The begin half of a split transition, emitted right after a pass; the
matching RGBarrier (splitBeginAfter set) ends it before the pass at endOrder.

Declare resources. Transient textures/buffers may be aliased onto
shared memory when their lifetimes don't overlap; imported ones are
owned externally and never aliased.

members.name: PassExecuteFn
members.doc:
GPU body of a pass, run by the executor after its barriers. Fetches
physical images via the executor (GetImage). Empty for passes that
only declare dependencies in tests.

members.name: AddPass
members.signature: RGPass AddPass(const std::string& name, std::vector<RGAccess> reads, std::vector<RGAccess> writes, PassExecuteFn execute = {})
members.doc:
Add a pass that reads and writes the given resources (each in the
state the pass needs). Order of AddPass calls is the registration
order used as a stable tiebreak during scheduling.

members.name: SetCullDeadPasses
members.doc:
Dead-pass culling (R15), opt-in: drop passes whose writes never reach
an imported resource, transitively. OFF by default because the unified
frame graph's slicing contract indexes Order() with compile-time
constants — culling would shift them — and its pass callbacks may have
side effects the resource model can't see (persistent-image copies).
A pass declaring NO writes is treated as side-effect-only and kept.

members.name: SetAsyncCompute
members.doc:
Async compute, opt-in per pass (set before Compile). The executor may
record a flagged pass on the async-compute lane — forked with the
graphics hand-off, so the lane sees everything recorded before it — and
joins the lane right before the first later pass that conflicts with it.
The body must record compute or copy work only, and every image it
touches must be lane-reachable (no attachment usage); otherwise, and on
a backend without a lane, the pass runs inline with identical results.

members.name: SetAluHeavy
members.doc:
Overlap placement, as UE schedules it: async work belongs beside
raster/ROP-bound graphics (shadow depths, prepass, G-Buffer), not beside
ALU-heavy compute or full-screen shading, where the two queues only
fight over the same ALUs. A pass marked here is such a pass, and a lane
joins before it even when it reads nothing the lane wrote.

members.name: SetForceAsyncEligible
members.doc:
r.RDG.AsyncCompute 2 (testing): at Compile, every compute-shaped pass —
one with no render-target or depth-write access and at least one write —
is treated as if it had opted in. Set by the executor's cvar reader.

members.name: AsyncJoinOrder
members.doc:
Execution-order index of the first pass after `pass` that must wait for
it: one that reads or writes what it writes, writes what it reads, first
uses a transient (whose memory it may share) while `pass` touches one,
or is itself async. RG_INVALID when nothing later in the graph does —
the executor then joins at the end of the slice.

members.name: SplitBeginsAfter
members.doc:
Split transitions that may begin right after `pass` executes: transient
textures only, never out of Undefined (a placed transient's activation)
or UnorderedAccess (its compute barrier), never touching an async pass.

members.name: Compile
members.doc:
Schedule + compute barriers + aliasing. Returns false if the
dependencies form a cycle (Order() is left empty).

members.name: Order
members.doc: Passes in execution order.

members.name: BarriersBefore
members.doc: Barriers to emit immediately before the pass executes.

members.name: AliasGroup
members.doc:
Memory-alias group of a transient resource: two transient resources
in the same group share backing memory (disjoint lifetimes). Imported
resources and any resource with no group return RG_INVALID.

members.name: Lifetime
members.signature: void Lifetime(RGResource resource, uint32_t& firstUse, uint32_t& lastUse) const
members.doc:
Inclusive lifetime [firstUse, lastUse] in execution-order indices, or
{RG_INVALID, RG_INVALID} if the resource is never used.

members.name: ResourceUsage
members.doc:
Aggregate usage flags a resource needs across all its accesses
(RenderTarget→ColorAttachment, ShaderRead→Sampled, Transfer*→…), so
the executor can allocate a backing image with the right usage.

members.name: TransientBytes
members.signature: void TransientBytes(uint64_t& logical, uint64_t& physical) const
members.doc:
VRAM accounting for transient textures: `logical` is what a naive
one-image-per-resource allocation would cost; `physical` is what the
aliased allocation (one image per group, sized to its largest member)
actually costs. logical - physical is the memory the aliasing reclaims.

other (non-graph) passes run in the gaps between slices.

Whether the active backend may run with the render and RHI threads:
Vulkan and D3D12 record per-thread lists, D3D11 queues other threads'
writes for the frame they belong to (r.D3D11.RenderThread), Metal still
waits each frame slot out on the game thread.

members.name: RegisterStaticCacheRelease
members.doc:
A live API switch destroys the device under higher-tier modules that park
GPU objects in file-static caches (GPUMesh morph compute, the underwater
pass) — the RHI cannot reach those, and their own teardown only runs at
engine/system shutdown. Each such module registers a releaser at load and
SetAPI drops the caches while the old device is still alive.

members.signature: static void OnWindowResize(uint32_t width, uint32_t height)

members.name: GetMainViewport
members.doc:
Per-window viewports (UE5 FRHIViewport model). The main window is
viewport 0 — GetMainViewport() wraps the swapchain + command buffer
GetSwapChain()/GetCurrentCommandBuffer() return, so those stay a
compatibility shim for the main viewport. Secondary windows (crash
reporter, tear-off tabs, tool windows) call CreateViewport with their
own native handle to get an independent swapchain + backbuffer + depth
+ sync, and drive their own BeginFrame/EndFrame/Present. DestroyViewport
drops the registry's reference once the owner is done with it.

members.name: ReleaseRetiredViewport
members.doc:
DestroyViewport for a viewport whose every frame the GPU has already
retired — one handed to SubmitDeferredRelease on its last present and
released from there. No idle wait: tearing a closed menu's swapchain
down with one stalled the editor for a GPU frame per wait.

members.name: SubmitDeferredRelease
members.doc:
Runs the release once the frames that may still read what it frees
have left the GPU (the DeferredDeleteQueue's frames-in-flight delay).

members.name: SetActiveViewport
members.doc:
Bind the window whose swapchain + command buffer the swapchain-facing
statics (BeginSwapChainRenderPass, Draw, GetSwapChain, ...) target.
Passing null restores the main viewport. Secondary windows bind
themselves for the duration of their own frame, then restore the main.
The bind is per thread: a window recording on the rendering thread is
invisible to the game thread reading the main swapchain meanwhile.

members.name: GetFrameCounter
members.doc:
Monotonic count of frames begun since Init — NOT the frames-in-flight
ring index GetCurrentFrameIndex returns. This is the frame IDENTITY the
vendor SDKs key on: a Streamline frame token, the Reflex/PCL latency
markers and the DLSS-G pacer must all name the same frame, or the
latency report is attributed to the wrong one and the interpolator
orders its history by a counter that wraps every few frames. One
counter, read here by everything that needs it.

members.name: GetDynamicRHI
members.doc:
The active graphics backend. Null before Init/after Shutdown. The
abstract RHI facades route their per-API work through this — it is
not a consumer-facing surface.

members.name: BeginRenderPass

members.doc: Begin/End rendering to an off-screen framebuffer (G-Buffer, shadow map, etc.)

members.name: BeginSwapChainRenderPass
members.doc: Begin/End rendering directly to the swapchain backbuffer

members.name: SuspendRenderPass
members.doc:
Suspend the render pass opened by the last Begin*RenderPass and resume
it later with loadOp=LOAD. A render pass may not begin while another
one is active, so a guest renderer that must draw into its OWN
framebuffers in the middle of a host-owned pass brackets that work
in Suspend/Resume. The host's
attachments keep their COLOR_ATTACHMENT layout across the gap, so no
barriers are emitted — only the passes the guest itself begins are
transitioned. Not reentrant: one suspension may be live at a time.

A dispatch whose inputs this frame uploaded with SetData and whose
output this frame's draws consume: recorded into the frame's command
stream (after the copies, before the draws, with the compute→graphics
barrier) whenever one is open, and submitted single-time otherwise.
DispatchImmediate from inside a frame is NOT that on D3D12 — its
single-time list runs ahead of the frame list that carries the copies,
so the kernel reads the previous contents. The meshlet vertex gather
did exactly this and read uninitialized page tables after a large
page-in: a garbage per-page source count looped a thread ~2^26 times
(DEVICE_HUNG on Sun Temple) or, when it read zeros, wrote nothing and
the frame drew grid and sky. Not for a dispatch followed by a CPU
readback: that still needs completion, i.e. DispatchImmediate.

Repeated calls overdraw — for non-overlapping viewports this is

the dynamic-resolution active extent when the source chain is
allocated larger than the frame rendered. 0 = the whole image.

members.doc:

recreation); stays 0 when the surface offers no HDR formats.

members.name: SetSceneHDRMode
members.doc:

sets this to the negotiated swapchain mode so the SceneRenderer
tonemapper encodes for the display; the editor
never sets it — its scenes stay SDR and are mapped to paper white by
the overlay composite instead.

members.name: BeginOverlayTarget
members.doc:

(identical to BeginSwapChainRenderPass(true) / EndSwapChainRenderPass);
with an HDR swapchain the overlay renders into an offscreen BGRA8
staging image and End composites it with the paper-white sRGB→HDR
encode. Call in place of the swapchain-pass pair around overlay draws.

members.name: AsyncComputeSupported
members.doc:
Async compute lane — a second hardware queue running compute work
concurrently with the graphics queue. Usage is a bracket around the
work plus one wait before whatever consumes it:

if (Renderer::BeginAsyncCompute()) { ...record...; Renderer::EndAsyncCompute(); }
else { ...record the same work inline... }
...graphics passes that do not touch it...
Renderer::WaitAsyncCompute();   // before the first consumer

BeginAsyncCompute returns false when the backend has no second queue,
a lane is already open, or a render pass is recording — the caller then
records inline and gets identical results without the overlap. The
recording calls in between are the ordinary ones: the lane works by
swapping the command buffer the facade records into.

SCHEDULING POLICY. What may go on the lane is not a matter of taste —
the queues are ordered in ONE direction only (lane signals, graphics
waits), so:
1. A lane pass may read only what was finished before the lane opened
or in an earlier frame. There is no graphics→lane wait; a lane pass
that samples something this frame's graphics queue is still writing
reads a torn resource, and no barrier inside either command buffer
can express that ordering.
2. Nothing recorded on the graphics queue between the lane's open and
the wait may touch what the lane writes. That span is exactly the
overlap window, and it is unsynchronized by construction.
3. The wait goes immediately before the first consumer, between passes.
Inside a render pass or a GPU timestamp scope the backend cannot
split the graphics submit (both hold the raw command buffer), so the
wait silently degrades to a whole-frame wait — correct, but the
overlap is lost.
4. Every resource the lane touches must be reachable from the compute
queue. On Vulkan the RHI marks compute-reachable resources
CONCURRENT at creation; an attachment-usage image is NOT one of
them, and handing the lane a render target is a queue-ownership
violation the backend logs rather than papers over.
EndFrame waits for an outstanding lane the caller forgot to wait on, so
a skipped consumer degrades to a stall, never to a race.

waitForGraphicsSoFar lifts rule 1 for ONE bracket: the graphics work
recorded up to this point is submitted immediately and the lane's submit
waits for it, so the lane may read what those passes wrote. It is opt-in
per call because it costs a graphics submit at the open and shrinks the
overlap window to what is recorded AFTER the bracket; the default false
is the one-way lane every existing caller gets. It returns false — no
lane, record inline — on a backend without the reverse primitive or
while a GPU scope holds the command buffer the split would end.

members.name: AsyncComputeGraphicsHandoffSupported
members.doc:
Whether a lane can be opened with waitForGraphicsSoFar at all on the
live backend, for a caller that wants to choose its pass layout rather
than discover the refusal.

members.name: AsyncComputeInFlight
members.doc:
True between EndAsyncCompute and the wait that consumes it — the window
in which lane work and graphics work are executing concurrently.

members.name: AsyncComputeSplitWaitCount
members.doc:
How many lane submissions the graphics queue actually waited for behind a
SPLIT submit (real in-frame overlap) versus folded into the frame's own
submit (no in-frame overlap). Counters are process-lifetime; the split
count staying at zero is the signal that the lane is recording into a
second buffer and nothing more.

members.name: AsyncComputeGraphicsHandoffCount
members.doc:
How many lanes were opened with the graphics→lane hand-off. Zero means
the reverse primitive is built and nothing has asked for it — which is
the intended state until a pass qualifies for it.

members.name: NoteGpuScopeOpened
members.doc:
GPU timestamp scopes hold the raw command buffer they opened on, so a
split submit underneath one would end a buffer the scope still writes
into. GpuScope reports its depth here and the lane refuses to split
while any scope is open.

members.name: ReloadShaders
members.doc:
WaitIdle → drop the VFS read cache → re-read SPIR-V for every live
shader → recreate every live pipeline. Must be called OUTSIDE frame
recording (before BeginFrame). Returns the number of shaders whose
bytecode actually changed.

types.name: Renderer::FTransitionCounters
types.doc:
Transition requests, split by who issued them: the render-graph
executor's barrier walk, or code recording outside it (pass bodies run
by the graph included, since their barriers are still hand-placed).
Cumulative across the process; a frame's share is the difference of
two reads. Requests, not barriers — a request for the state an image is
already in records nothing.

members.doc:
Out-of-line on purpose: MOWO_API is dllexport in every module that
defines MW_BUILD_DLL, so an in-class initialiser would define and export
the storage once PER DLL and a switch would only ever move RHI.dll's
copy. One definition lives in RendererAPI.cpp; everyone else imports it.

types.name: FRHIApiCeiling
types.doc:
What each graphics API can EVER express, independent of the GPU/driver
underneath — the static ceiling next to the live RendererCapabilities.
The editor uses the pair to decide between hiding a control (the API can
never do it) and greying it (this GPU/build can't right now); future
backends inherit the policy by adding a column here.

members.name: SupportsRayTracingPipeline
members.doc:
Ray-tracing PIPELINE state objects + a shader binding table, the axis
SupportsRayTracing does NOT cover. Metal traces through
intersection_query and has no pipeline/SBT concept at all, so a
control that needs one (r.RTReflections.Pipeline) must be hidden
there rather than offered and silently falling back to the inline
query — which is what the missing predicate cost.

members.name: SupportsUpscaler
members.signature: static bool SupportsUpscaler(RendererAPIType api, UpscalerType type)
members.doc:
Which upscaler an API can host at all. The FSR providers exist for
D3D12 and Vulkan only, Streamline carries DLSS and XeSS ships runtimes
on the three Windows APIs, and MetalFX is Metal's alone. The engine's
own (None/TAA/Spatial/TSR) run everywhere. Whether THIS device can is
IUpscaler::IsUpscalerSupported.

members.name: SupportsFrameGenBackend
members.signature: static bool SupportsFrameGenBackend(RendererAPIType api, EFrameGenBackend backend)
members.doc:
Which frame-generation backend an API can host. XeSS-FG's only shape is
a DXGI proxy swapchain, so Vulkan can never run it; FSR3 and DLSS-G wrap
both D3D12 and Vulkan presents; MetalFX is Metal's interpolator.

members.name: SupportsReflex
members.doc:
NVIDIA Reflex rides Streamline, which has D3D11, D3D12 and Vulkan
runtimes and no Metal one.

members.name: SupportsLowLatencyBackend
members.signature: static bool SupportsLowLatencyBackend(RendererAPIType api, ELowLatencyBackend backend)
members.doc:
Which latency runtime an API can host. Reflex as above; the engine drives
AMD Anti-Lag 2 through its D3D12 driver extension and Intel XeLL through
xell_d3d12, so both are D3D12-only here.

members.name: SupportsAsyncCompute
members.doc:
A second hardware queue that runs compute concurrently with graphics.
D3D11's immediate context is the whole submission model — there is no
queue object to submit to, so no driver will ever expose one. The other
three can: Vulkan compute queue families, D3D12 compute command queues,
Metal's untyped command queues. This is the API ceiling only — ask
Renderer::AsyncComputeSupported() whether the LIVE backend built one.

members.name: SupportsVariableRateShading
members.doc:
Image-based variable-rate shading: a per-tile rate image the rasterizer
reads (D3D12 VRS Tier 2 shading-rate image, Vulkan
VK_KHR_fragment_shading_rate attachment). D3D11 has no VRS at all, and
Metal's rasterization-rate maps are a different model (a warped
viewport, not a per-tile rate) that this path does not drive — both
hide the control. Whether THIS device has Tier 2 / the attachment
feature is RendererCapabilities::SupportsVariableRateShadingImage.

transfer queue (Vulkan: CONCURRENT sharing across the graphics +
transfer families when they differ; other backends ignore it). Set by
the texture streamer on its staged-assembly targets.

members.name: ExternalDepth
members.doc:
If set, use this existing depth image instead of creating a new one.
Allows sharing depth between framebuffers (e.g., GBuffer depth → HDR target).

members.name: ExternalColors
members.doc:
If set, wrap these existing images as the color attachments instead
of allocating new ones (one per Attachments format). This is how a
render-pass pass renders into render-graph-allocated (and aliased)
targets: the graph owns the memory, the framebuffer is just the
binding.

members.name: GraphManaged
members.doc:
When true, Begin/EndRenderPass do NOT transition this framebuffer's
attachments — the render graph executor owns every transition (via
Renderer::TransitionImage), so its state model stays authoritative.
Used for graph-driven passes; default keeps the self-managing
behaviour every existing pass relies on.

members.name: ClearOnCreate
members.doc:
Clear the color attachments to black + transition them to ShaderRead
at creation (single-time command, GPU-synchronous). For temporal
history ping-pongs: the first frame samples DEFINED black instead of
an UNDEFINED image, and a dropped warm-up command buffer can no
longer leave the tracked layout ahead of the GPU.

members.name: ClearColor
members.doc:
Clear color for CLEAR-loadOp render passes on this framebuffer's color
attachments. Default stays opaque black — the transparent-black variant
exists for the overlay HDR staging target (UI composited by alpha).

members.name: ShadingRateImage
members.doc:
Variable-rate shading: a rate image (ImageUsage::ShadingRate, R8UI, one
texel per RendererCapabilities::ShadingRateTileSize pixels, already in
ImageState::ShadingRateSource) the rasterizer reads for this pass.
Ignored where the device has no image-based VRS. The backend resets the
rate at EndRenderPass, so no later pass inherits it.

members.name: LoadDepth
members.doc:
A CLEAR begin still clears the colour attachments but LOADS the depth
attachment. For a pass whose depth was laid down by an earlier depth
prepass: clearing it would throw the prepass away, and not clearing the
colours would leave last frame's G-buffer under every pixel the pass
skips.

types.name: FGpuMemoryStats
types.doc:
Live GPU memory as the driver reports it. "Local" is memory on the device
itself (VRAM on a discrete card), "shared" is system memory the driver maps
for the GPU. Budget is what the OS currently lets this process use, which
shrinks when other applications take VRAM, so it is the number an
over-budget decision has to read, not the card capacity. Everything is 0
when the backend has no driver query (Valid stays false).

members.name: UploadRingUploads
members.doc:
The backend's shared upload staging ring: uploads it served, uploads
that took a dedicated staging resource instead (too big, or the ring
full of copies still in flight), and bytes not yet retired. All 0 on a
backend without a ring.

members.name: UploadAsyncSubmits
members.doc:
Create-with-data uploads that were submitted without the CPU waiting
for them (D3D12 r.D3D12.AsyncUploads, Vulkan r.Vulkan.AsyncUploads); 0
where every upload waits.

members.name: UploadCopyQueueSubmits
members.doc:
Create-with-data uploads copied on the COPY queue with a GPU-side wait
on the direct queue (D3D12, r.D3D12.CopyQueueUploads); 0 elsewhere.

members.name: MaxPushConstantBytes
members.doc:
Vulkan's maxPushConstantsSize; every other backend keeps the portable
floor (FPushConstantBudget::PortableBytes), which is also what the
renderer is built to.

members.name: SupportsRayQuery
members.doc: VK_KHR_acceleration_structure + ray_query enabled

members.name: SupportsRayTracingPipeline
members.doc:
Ray-tracing PIPELINE state objects + a shader binding table
(VK_KHR_ray_tracing_pipeline / DXR CreateStateObject). Strictly
narrower than SupportsRayQuery: Metal reports ray query through
intersection_query but has no pipeline/SBT equivalent at all, and a
Vulkan driver may expose acceleration structures + ray query without
the pipeline extension. Never infer one bit from the other.

members.name: SupportsShaderInt64
members.doc: 64-bit shader integers (RT hit fetch via buffer device address)

members.name: SupportsInt64Atomics
members.doc:
64-bit atomics on storage buffers (SM6.6 on D3D12, shaderBufferInt64Atomics
on Vulkan). The compute point rasteriser packs depth and colour into one
word and resolves a pixel with a single InterlockedMin; without this it
falls back to the splat draw. D3D11 and Metal report false.

members.name: SupportsDrawIndirectCount
members.doc:
Count-buffer indirect draws (vkCmdDrawIndexedIndirectCount / ExecuteIndirect
with a count buffer). D3D11 and Metal have no equivalent; every backend
has DispatchIndirect.

members.name: SupportsAsyncCompute
members.doc:
A second hardware queue this DEVICE exposes and this backend actually
built a lane on. FRHIApiCeiling::SupportsAsyncCompute says only that the
API could express one; this is the per-device half, and the only place a
vendor whose compute queue exists but runs no faster than its graphics
queue can be recorded.

members.name: SupportsFSR
members.doc:
Vendor-SDK features the backend was built with (pre-device: compile
gates; post-device the runtime probes may still narrow them).

members.name: CheapPerDrawIndirect
members.doc:
Whether one indirect draw per mesh costs about what the direct draw
does. False on D3D12, where each is an ExecuteIndirect: the Sun Temple's
GPU-culled GBuffer spent 5.5 ms of GPU on 2,100 of them against 1.0 ms
drawn directly (Vulkan: 0.6). The renderer then draws the classic path
directly from the CPU frustum test and keeps GPU culling for meshlets.

members.name: SupportsVariableRateShadingImage
members.doc:
Image-based variable-rate shading on this device: D3D12 VRS Tier 2, or
Vulkan's attachmentFragmentShadingRate. The tile is the pixel extent
one rate-image texel covers. FRHIApiCeiling::SupportsVariableRateShading
is the API half.

types.name: ImageState
types.doc:
Abstract image usage state for the backend-agnostic transition API.
Each maps to a concrete layout + sync scope per backend (image
layout / D3D resource state / Metal usage). Transitioning between
two distinct states emits a barrier.

members.doc: no defined contents (discard on transition out)

types.name: FShaderPath
types.doc:
The runtime half of the virtual shader paths MBT compiles from. Sources are
named "/Engine/Private/GBuffer/GBufferFill.hlsl", "/Plugin/<Name>/Private/…",
"/Project/Private/…" or "/Test/…"; the archives key their blobs by a short
name with the root folded in, which is what every Shader::Create call has
always passed:

/Engine/Private/GBuffer/GBufferFill.hlsl     -> GBuffer/GBufferFill
/Engine/StandaloneRenderer/Arc/ArcStandard  -> Arc/ArcStandard
/Plugin/Foo/Private/Bar.comp.hlsl           -> Plugin/Foo/Bar
/Project/Private/Water.hlsl                 -> Project/Water
/Test/PermutationTest.comp.hlsl             -> Test/PermutationTest

The engine root keeps its keys bare so hundreds of existing names and every
packed archive stay valid; any other root is prefixed so a plugin's
"Lighting/X" can never shadow the engine's. MBT's ShaderSourceMap.BlobKeyFor
applies the same rule at cook time; the two must agree.

members.name: ReadBackLatched
members.signature: virtual bool ReadBackLatched(void* dest, uint64_t size, uint64_t offset = 0)
members.doc:
Frame-latent readback for per-frame consumers. Returns what the previous
use of this frames-in-flight slot copied out and queues the next copy
into the frame's own command list, so the CPU never waits on the GPU —
a blocking ReadBack per frame costs a full queue drain on D3D12 and
Metal. The value is up to two ring cycles old, and one buffer must be
read with the same range every frame. False (dest untouched) until the
slot holds a completed copy. Backends whose ReadBack is already a plain
map read keep this default.

members.name: OnPresentEnqueued
members.doc:
Called on the RENDERING thread at the moment the frame's submit +
present are handed to the RHI thread (before they execute). A backend
whose SubmitFrame/Present read per-frame sync objects through a frame
cursor snapshots the cursor here and advances it — so the next
BeginFrame on the rendering thread uses the NEXT slot while the
in-flight submit keeps this one, instead of both touching the same
fence/semaphore concurrently. Default no-op for backends without a
cursor (D3D11 immediate).

ONLY Renderer::Present / PresentDeferred call this — the main viewport's
path. RHIViewport (every secondary window: tool windows, tear-offs,
popups) does not, so a backend that needs this hook to keep its acquire
and its present in step is silently broken on every window but the main
one. That was real: the Vulkan swapchain's cursor never moved for a
secondary viewport, so each of its presents named image 0 whatever the
acquire had returned. Pair inside BeginFrame/Present instead, and treat
this hook as an optimization a backend may ignore.

types.name: FUploadRingAllocator
types.doc:
Offset bookkeeping for a backend's staging ring: one persistently mapped
upload buffer that create-with-data and static-buffer uploads carve their
staging out of instead of allocating a fresh upload resource each. A block
is live from Allocate until Retire, which the backend calls once the GPU
finished the copy; the tail advances over retired blocks in allocation
order, so a block retired early just waits for the ones ahead of it. A
request that does not fit answers false and the caller falls back to its
own staging resource — the ring is a fast path, never a dependency.
Not thread-safe: the owning backend ring locks around it.
